assignments.reason: The essential nature of this concept is the bond/attachment to the tzaddik. It is not a quality of malkhut or humility — it is the act of connecting oneself to the tzaddik, whose essential nature is the great light of Yom Tov (Package 2). The Torah states (line 17): 'עִקַּר הַהִתְקַשְּׁרוּת הוּא אַהֲבָה — שֶׁיֹּאהַב אֶת הַצַּדִּיק אַהֲבָה שְׁלֵמָה.' The attachment IS the relationship to the tzaddik. It produces humility (Package 1 result), but it IS a tzaddik-domain concept.

Teshuvah (repentance/return) in Torah #135 is the active spiritual mechanism of Yom Tov as a day of judgment. The Torah states (line 21-22): 'יוֹם טוֹב נִקְרָא תְּשׁוּבַת הַשָּׁנָה... וְצָרִיךְ לָשׁוּב בִּתְשׁוּבָה.' Teshuvah's essential nature here is the judgment/din dimension of the holy calendar — its direct effect is the liberation of malkhut dikdusha from the klipot. Din, yirah, and malkhut are all in Package 1; teshuvah in this Torah is the temporal-spiritual expression of that same domain of judgment and return to holy kingship.

Same essential nature as 'לשוב בתשובה' — teshuvah as the active spiritual dimension of the Yom Tov judgment cycle. The Torah explicitly ties it to the liberation of malkhut: 'גְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמְּקָרֶבֶת אֶת הַגְּאֻלָּה — שֶׁנִּגְאָלִין עַל־יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה מֵהַמַּלְכוּת דִּקְלִפּוֹת.' Teshuvah IS the return of the divine kingdom — it belongs to the malkhut/din/yirah domain.

This is the Torah's practical advice — a segulah (remedy) for escaping arrogance. Its essential nature is a pathway to humility (ענוה), which is in Package 1. The Torah opens with this: 'סְגֻלָּה לְהִנָּצֵל מִגַּדְלוּת — לְכַבֵּד אֶת הַיָּמִים טוֹבִים.' The remedy's goal IS humility — it belongs to the ענוה/malkhut domain by its essential purpose and nature. It produces humility; it is OF the humility domain.

This compound node describes the act of receiving Yom Tov explicitly identified as Binah. The additions file already placed 'יום טוב' in Package 1 because Yom Tov as Mochin deImma/Binah is the supernal source of humility. This node's essential nature is Yom Tov-as-Binah — the cognitive/spiritual dimension whose gates Moshe attained and through which he became the most humble of men. It belongs to the Binah/humility/malkhut domain (Package 1), not the tzaddik/light domain (Package 2).

assignments.node_id: כשמקבל ומכבד את הימים טובים, ומקבל אור הגדול של יום־טוב, שהוא בחינת צדיק
assignments.reason: This compound node explicitly identifies the act of receiving Yom Tov as receiving 'the great light of Yom Tov, which is a bechina of the tzaddik.' The node's own text declares its nature: it IS the experience of the tzaddik's light via Yom Tov. 'אור הגדול של יום טוב' and 'צדיק' are both Package 2 nodes. This node describes engagement with that same luminous, tzaddik-centered reality.

The act of receiving the holiness of Yom Tov. 'קדשת יום טוב' is a core node of Package 2, where it is a bechina of the tzaddik. This node describes the reception of that same holiness. Its essential nature is in the tzaddik/Yom Tov holiness domain. The proof text (line 29): 'וּכְשֶׁמְּקַבְּלִים קְדֻשַּׁת יוֹם-טוֹב, יֵשׁ לוֹ עֲנָוָה וְשִׁפְלוּת' — it produces humility, but it IS the reception of the sacred light.

assignments.node_id: לכבד את הימים טובים, ולקבל יום טוב בשמחה ובהרחבת הלב כפי יכלתו
assignments.reason: The practical action of honoring and receiving the festivals with joy and expansiveness. This is the concrete form of engaging with Yom Tov's holiness. The Torah equates Yom Tov's holiness with the tzaddik ('עִקַּר כֹּחַ קְדֻשַּׁת יוֹם-טוֹב הוּא תָּלוּי בַּצַּדִּיקִים'). The act of honoring and joyfully receiving Yom Tov is therefore an act of engaging with the tzaddik's light. Its nature is in the Yom Tov/tzaddik domain (Package 2), even though its effect is humility (Package 1).

The ability to sense/perceive the holiness of Yom Tov. This is the experiential dimension of קדשת יום טוב, which is a core Package 2 node. The node describes the subjective capacity to perceive the tzaddik's light as manifested in Yom Tov — its essential nature is squarely in the Yom Tov holiness/tzaddik domain.

The capacity to receive the holiness of Yom Tov. Essentially the same as 'יוכל להרגיש קדשת יום־טוב' — a variant expression of the same reality. קדשת יום טוב is Package 2; the capacity to receive it belongs to the same domain.

assignments.node_id: יוצא המלכות מבין הקלפות, ונתבטל ממשלתם
assignments.reason: The liberation of malkhut dikdusha from among the klipot and the annulment of their rule. Its essential nature is about MALKHUT — the holy kingdom emerging from captivity. מלכות is the dominant node of Package 1. This node describes the positive outcome for malkhut: it exits its exile among the four evil kingdoms. Though the klipot are mentioned, the node's subject is the liberation of holy malkhut — a good-domain concept in the malkhut/yirah cluster.

Being redeemed through teshuvah from the kingdom of the klipot. Same essential domain as 'יוצא המלכות מבין הקלפות' — this describes the geulah (redemption) of the holy malkhut from the evil shells. The subject is the positive act of redemption through teshuvah; both teshuvah and malkhut belong to Package 1. The klipot are mentioned as what one is redeemed FROM, but the node's nature is the positive redemption itself.

The annulment of arrogance. This describes the state where gaavah (arrogance) dissolves — the positive result that IS humility. When arrogance is annulled, what remains is ענוה (humility), which is a core Package 1 node. The essential nature of 'the annulment of arrogance' is the emergence of humility — it is the negative formulation of the same positive reality described by ענוה. Polarity is good because the node describes the positive outcome (arrogance defeated), not the evil trait itself.

His arrogance is annulled — personalized variant of 'נתבטל הגדלות.' Same essential nature: the emergence of personal humility through the dissolution of arrogance. This is ענוה/שפלות experienced by the individual. Package 1 domain.

Humility and lowliness — a compound of ענוה (already in Package 1) and שפלות (lowliness, a synonym/intensification of ענוה). The source text (line 29) presents them together: 'יֵשׁ לוֹ עֲנָוָה וְשִׁפְלוּת.' Same essential nature as ענוה. Core Package 1 concept.
